claim: TubeArchivist schedules its subscription rescan with a cron-like minute/hour/day-of-week format, cannot run more than once per hour, and warns frequent schedules risk YouTube throttling.
quote: the first value is the minute, second is the hour and third is day of the week as a number... the scheduler doesn't support schedules that trigger more than once per hour... Avoid an unnecessary or frequent schedule to reduce likelihood of being blocked or throttled by YouTube.

claim: TubeArchivist's Rescan Subscriptions task scans subscribed channels and playlists for new videos, shorts and streams and queues missing ones; meant to run once per day.
quote: The Rescan Subscriptions feature will start a background task to look for new videos from the channels and playlists you are subscribed to... The rescan task is meant to be run once per day.

claim: Pinchflat uses interval-based (not cron) indexing where the next index is scheduled only after the current completes, supports Title Filter Regex, a Download Cutoff Date (YYYY-MM-DD) and min/max duration filters, fully indexes a channel once then only checks for new media, and self-throttles concurrent yt-dlp operations.
quote: the next indexing gets scheduled only after the current one completes... it's only fully indexed once. After that point indexing only looks for new media... Pinchflat is configured to only perform a certain number of operations at the same time.

claim: ytdl-sub has no built-in poller; scheduling is external via cron, using a CRON_SCHEDULE env var in Docker (e.g. "0 */6 * * *") or a host crontab entry.
quote: Enable cron support by setting a cron schedule in the CRON_SCHEDULE environment variable... CRON_SCHEDULE: "0 */6 * * *"

claim: ytdl-sub tracks downloaded videos in a per-subscription download-archive JSON and uses date_range plus break_on_existing to stop at already-downloaded media, so back-catalog is grabbed by widening the date range then re-enabling break_on_existing for fast incremental runs.
quote: decides what files have already been downloaded by entries in the download archive file... break_on_existing... will stop downloading additional metadata/videos if the video exists in your download archive.

claim: TubeSync gives each source an index frequency (interval at which it checks a channel/playlist for new media), recommended kept as long as possible up to 24 hours; it also supports a minimum-resolution cutoff and retries with back-off.
quote: Index frequency is the duration between indexes of the source... TubeSync recommends keeping the index frequency as long as possible, up to 24 hours.

claim: MeTube now supports subscriptions: it subscribes to channels/playlists, periodically checks for new items and auto-queues uploads, with SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL (default 60 min) and SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_PLAYLIST_END (default 50 newest).
quote: Subscribe to channels and playlists, periodically check for new items, and queue new uploads automatically... SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL: Default minutes between automatic checks for each subscription. Defaults to 60.

claim: MeTube's subscription/auto-download capability was a long-standing feature request (issue #76) only implemented in recent 2026 releases.
quote: Monitor subscriptions for auto-download

claim: TubeArchivist supports a YouTube cookie that turns Watch Later and Liked Videos into regular subscribable/downloadable playlists; validity is checked by whether yt-dlp can read your private Liked Videos playlist, and the single per-instance cookie is stored in Redis and shared across all users.
quote: A cookie is considered as valid if yt-dlp is able to access your private Liked Videos playlist... There is only one cookie per Tube Archivist instance, and this will be shared between all users.

claim: TubeArchivist warns YouTube has a detection mechanism that invalidates cookies used outside a browser, and that the cookie carries the Google account access token and must be treated like a password.
quote: It appears that YT has some detection mechanism that will invalidate your cookie if it's being used outside of a browser... Treat that data with utmost care, as you would any other password or credential.

claim: PinchFlat takes a cookies.txt at /config/extras/cookies.txt with a per-source Cookie Behaviour setting, and its wiki warns yt-dlp no longer recommends YouTube cookies because they can trigger IP bans.
quote: yt-dlp no longer recommends using YouTube cookies since they can cause YouTube to issue IP bans.

claim: TubeSync (v0.10+) accepts a Netscape cookies file; users have pulled their Liked Videos playlist with it, with the explicit caveat that this identifies the Google account as using TubeSync and is entirely at the user's own risk.
quote: Using cookies exported from your browser that is authenticated to YouTube identifies your Google account as using TubeSync, which may result in potential account impacts and is entirely at your own risk.

claim: In 2026 Chrome 127+ app-bound encryption breaks external cookie extraction, Firefox's plain SQLite store is the only reliably working source, yt-dlp OAuth2 for YouTube is deprecated, and exported cookies expire in roughly two weeks.
quote: Firefox doesn't encrypt cookies... Chrome 127+ ... app-bound encryption that binds decryption keys to the Chrome binary itself... yt-dlp OAuth2 — YouTube deprecated this method.

claim: ytdl-sub can download a YouTube playlist (including Watch Later / Liked Videos via a cookiefile in ytdl_options) but automatically removing items dropped from the source playlist is still an open feature request.
quote: Sync Capability: Automatically remove items that are not in a playlist anymore

claim: TubeArchivist uses Elasticsearch to index titles, descriptions, subtitles and comments, with filters by language (ISO 639), subtitle source and channel, plus grid/table views.
quote: search interface includes advanced filtering options, such as searching by language using ISO 639 codes, filtering by subtitle source ... limiting searches to specific channels

claim: ytdl-sub is CLI-first; its only browser interface is a GUI Docker image built on LinuxServer's code-server, exposing a VS Code web editor and terminal for editing configs, not a media UI.
quote: The GUI image is based on LSIO's docker-code-server image to provide you full management of ytdl-sub, such as file editing and terminal access, all within your browser using the VS Code web UI
